Based on the mentioned tests, the expected results are obtained, which can become an innovative design for a new skin cancer detection device that improves efficiency in conducting examinations.

articleTitle: Capturing Optimum Result of The Hopfield Neural Network for Linear and Quadratic Programming
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In this paper, an expansion of Hopfield neural network for linear and quadratic programming is presented. Not converging to global minimum, converging to local minimum or not converging at all is an essential issue of the Hopfield neural network. While simulating a simple VLSI implementation of the Hopfield neural network, it was observed that during transition of the output vector in the state space, the output occasionally passes through points that are in the allowed region of the linear and quadratic programming problem and also, close to the global minimum of the network. These points are usually better than some of the local minima that will be obtained in the steady state. Due to this observation, an additional circuit is designed and added to Hopfield neural network to trap such an optimum output vector. The captured output in the offered solution will be the most possible optimum output of the network.

articleTitle: Review of IPv6 Mitigation Techniques for Enterprise Local Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: IPv6 was built to improve on existing IPv4 protocol and it is known to have multiple benefits over IPv4. One of the biggest advantage is the large address space which would solve the issue of address scarcity that is associated with IPv4. Another benefit that has been marketed is the security enhancements but new protocols being introduced by IPv6 also pose security challenges. In this regard, multiple studies have been conducted to find and test mitigation techniques related to IPv6 threats. Research has also been conducted to analyze why IPv6 has a slow adoption rate and it has been found that organizations do not feel the need to deploy it in their networks. Furthermore, they identify IPv6 as a complex protocol and challenging to implement. It has also been discussed that the IPv6 protocol is not being deployed widely due to security concerns. This study thus concentrates on the various techniques to address IPv6 threats in local enterprise networks. In this paper, we will analyze several measures to secure the IPv6 local area networks and their strengths as well as their limitations will be highlighted. This will help organizations obtain a better overview of what need to be considered while deploying IPv6 in their networks. The study also helps to identify the issues that still need to be further tackled and allows future researchers to direct their research pathway.

articleTitle: Research on TSN Fronthaul for Converged 5G Transport
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: With the expansion of 5G, the demand for intensive deployment and low cost makes the fronthaul network change from D-RAN to C-RAN mode, and the construction of 5G fronthaul network faces enormous challenges. This paper first introduces the evolution of the fronthaul network and the time-sensitive network (TSN) in the fronthaul network, and proposes the converged deployment architecture based on TSN fronthaul network, and then analyzes the service quality and advantages and disadvantages of the traditional and TSN-based fronthaul network. Next, it describes the comparative test scheme and data analysis of the two scenarios of TSN-based Ethernet and optical fiber in 5G fronthaul network. The conclusion provides a basis for the feasibility of TSN fronthaul for converged 5G transport and promotes the deployment of TSN-based Ethernet carrying 5G fronthaul network.

articleTitle: Comparison between Conventional and Quantum-Based P-Median Optimization for Energy Consumption in Iot Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Impressive advances in wireless communications and microelectronics have paved the way for the development of low-cost multifunctional sensors. As a direct result, the Internet of Things (IoT) has become a must-have technology in many crucial fields, including the environment, security, industry, logistics and agronomy. However, IoT-based applications involve many challenges in terms of routing, energy efficiency, security, quality of service (QoS), reliability, scalability, heterogeneity and congestion. In this paper, the energy consumption and efficiency problem in these networks is tackled. This problem is formulated as a p-median based mathematical model and solved using two different methods: a classical exact method and a new quantum-inspired metaheuristic (QIC). The latter offers energy savings of up to 15,48% and outperforms the classical method in terms of algorithmic complexity, making it highly suitable for real-world IoT network applications.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection System (IDS) of Multiclassification IoT by using Pipelining and an Efficient Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has quickly advanced and been incorporated into many different fields. With the use of IoT technology, gadgets can receive, process, and send data automatically. IoT has been rapidly accepted in many important fields since it makes life easier and increases service quality, yet it still faces significant privacy and security problems. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) could be implemented as a security feature to protect IoT networks from a variety of cyberattacks. This study suggests using IDS to defend against a wide range of cyberattacks on IoT systems. The suggested approach makes use of the Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) as well as Extra Trees (ExT) as efficient algorithms of classification. Also, the study uses the pipeline to put together several cross-validated phases while selecting various parameters to increase the detection rate. One dataset is utilized for evaluating and analyzing the performance outcomes so as to validate the efficiency of the suggested IDS approach. The evaluation findings show that the suggested IDS methods may greatly increase detection performance results concerning accuracy rate, precision, F1-score, and recall while also improving detection efficiency.

articleTitle: Impedance-Based Online Stability Monitoring and Control of VSC-Based Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper proposes an impedance-based online stability monitoring and control method for VSC-based power systems. Specifically, the impedance model of the VSCs and the grid are constructed analytically for the operating points of the system at predetermined time intervals. Thereafter, using the dominant zeros of the determinant of the closed-loop admittance of the system, the so-called loop admittance-based stability criterion is utilized for real-time online monitoring. A higher-level control layer is augmented to adjust the power set points of the VSCs when the system approaches instability to ensure a stable and reliable operation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified on a VSC-based network with time-domain simulations in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Scale Mobile Base Robotic Manipulator for Indoor Painting Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The present investigation aims to develop a remotely controlled robotic manipulator for interior painting applications. The system incorporates an Arduino Mega microcontroller for motor control, a SolidWorks design for the mobile robotic arm, and MDF material with pulleys, gears, and bearings for the physical construction. A PCB in Altium is contemplated in the design, featuring the L298N motor controller and meeting manufacturing requirements, including a ground plane. A PID control scheme is implemented using measured motor parameters such as inertia (J), viscous friction (B), torque constant (KT), etc. It contemplates calculations for Jacobians, inverse kinematics, direct kinematics and trajectory planning. To provide a user-friendly interface, an application is developed using MIT App Inventor, which allows visualization of motor angles, end-effector position, and joystick-based control of motors, base engines. Bluetooth connectivity is established via a Bluetooth module for wireless control. The experimental results demonstrate the efficacy and feasibility of the developed robotic manipulator system.

articleTitle: FaceCrypt: Securing Workplaces Based on Facial Recognition and Visual Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Physical Access Control Systems (PACS) are essential in many industries, but they have often relied on single-factor authentication methods that are vulnerable to security threats. To address this, we introduce FaceCrypt, a dual-factor authentication framework that combines facial recognition with access cards using visual cryptography. FaceCrypt uses advanced deep-learning techniques to extract 128-dimensional facial features for accurate identification. A confidential QR code image is generated as the second authentication factor using visual cryptographic algorithms. This QR code contains individual user-specific random numbers, which are split into two shares. One share is stored in the access card and the other is stored in the database. When a user presents their access card, the two shares are combined to decrypt the QR code image. If the image is valid, the user is granted access. FaceCrypt provides significantly enhanced security over traditional PACS systems while maintaining operational efficiency. It is a promising new approach to physical access control that can help organizations protect their facilities and assets.

articleTitle: Fall Detection and Efficiency Enhancement via Wearable Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Thread In Motion is a company producing technology and pursuing innovation and is well known for its smart gloves. The main purpose of the company products is to combine humans and technology instead of replacing humans altogether, this way human-based mistakes are minimized, and the capabilities of the users are enhanced. The smart glove consists of two main parts, a device and a glove with a conductive thread inside. The said device includes different electronic and mechanical parts which are perfectly stabilized on a unique type of textile fabric designed considering human physiology. The goal of Thread In Motion is to integrate cutting-edge technologies into the smart glove and offer solutions for users in different industries. One of the innovative projects of the company is capturing and analyzing human motions using a combination of Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensors and Machine Learning Algorithms. The biggest challenge has been to differentiate between the fall of the device and the fall of a user which was achieved in this project. The current physical movements of the user are perfectly monitored and analyzed. This way it is planned to make it possible to develop an alarm system in case of a health emergency with a “man-down” feature and increase efficiency in workplaces such as warehouses. Considering IMU's integration into the device, this project offers an extra opportunity to increase the chance of survival and/or reduce the risk of permanent injury for the users and reduce human-based mistakes. This talk will focus on IMU sensors and their combined usage with Machine Learning Algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimal Design Considerations For Over Head Transmission Line (OHTL)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide a concise overview of the optimal design considerations for overhead transmission lines. The study aims to identify and analyze the key factors influencing the design of overhead transmission lines in order to achieve maximum performance and efficiency. The research focuses on various aspects such as tower design, and electrical parameters, aiming to optimize the overall design of transmission lines. The need for optimal design considerations arises from the increasing demand for electricity and the crucial role that transmission lines play in the power network. With the growing complexity of power grids and the requirement for reliable and efficient energy transmission, it is essential to explore and understand the factors that contribute to the optimal design of overhead transmission lines. Moreover, the research paper focuses on electrical parameters, such as line voltage, current carrying capacity, and power losses. These parameters significantly influence the transmission line's efficiency and performance including substation relay setting. By analyzing different electrical parameters and their impact on transmission line design, this research aims to provide guidelines for optimizing the electrical characteristics of overhead transmission lines. By examining tower design, and electrical parameters, this study aims to provide valuable insights and recommendations for engineers and designers involved in the planning and implementation of transmission line projects. The findings of this research will contribute to the development of more efficient and reliable overhead transmission line systems, ultimately benefiting the power sector and the overall energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Multifunctional, IoT-Enabled, Smart Portable Enclosures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This is a short perspective paper on an emerging topic. Portable enclosures with controlled atmosphere are useful in field surgery, disaster response, biotechnology, and other applications. Blending these technologies with AI and IoT capabilities could lead to the next generation of such devices. For example, future surgical drapes and enclosures may benefit from the use of IoT sensors and control. IoT connection to a remote center for operation monitoring and control could support decision making and analytics. Further, adding remote AI capabilities to predict conditions as they arise could open new applications, such as dynamic decision-making for casualty management based on clinical progression.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Graph Representation Techniques for Code Vulnerability Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)

authors.preferredName: Muhammad Irfan Elahee bin Mohd Illzam Elahee
authors.firstName: Muhammad Irfan Elahee bin Mohd Illzam

abstract: The surge in software development and products that use software have intensified the risk of software vulnerabilities. The difficulty of maintaining code security has been exacerbated by the growing software ecosystem and complexity of contemporary software systems. Code vulnerability detection is important in preventing these vulnerabilities, but current methods are time-consuming and may overlook certain vulnerabilities. Deep learning, specifically tree/graph-based neural network, may be a promising solution as it preserves hierarchical and structural information in code, leading to better performance in vulnerability detection. This research engages in a more comprehensive investigation in discussing different methods of code representation, including Abstract Syntax Trees (AST), Control Flow Graphs (CFG) and Program Dependence Graphs (PDG). These graphs undergo thorough analysis and are examined to pinpoint the critical information they extract and how it contributes to vulnerability detection. Notably, it is discovered that distinct graph representations excel at identifying different types of vulnerabilities. The information captured from each graph representations can be used to identify the type of vulnerability and differentiate vulnerable code from non-vulnerable code. Such finding lays the foundation for a more advanced software vulnerability detection tool based on graph representation of codes, offering software vulnerabilities can be efficiently addressed.

articleTitle: Toward Unveiling the Execution of Large-Scale Agile Project in Global Software Development: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Global Software Development (GSD) has emerged as a promising strategy for reducing software development costs. However, the adoption of GSD also brings forth various challenges. The geographical and socio-cultural dispersion of stakeholders can lead to ineffective communication and coordination, resulting in project delays. Moreover, executing large-scale agile projects in a global software development environment poses additional complexities, such as team coordination, customer collaboration, and knowledge transfer. This research aims to identify the key challenges faced in implementing large-scale agile projects in GSD environments and provide best practices to address these challenges. The state-of-the-art of this study is the identification of barriers and practices on scaling agile in a GSD environment and a thorough analysis and rationale on how the potential challenges could be eliminated through the practices. A systematic literature review (SLR) approach was performed using the Kitchenham framework to achieve the project objective. This paper executed six steps on planning review which led to 26 papers as primary studies that discuss the barriers faced by the teams and practices to overcome the barriers upon executing large-scale agile projects in GSD environments. The review process identified 24 challenges and 23 practices which were categorized into five categories: communication & collaboration, human resources management, project management, software methodology, and technology. This paper presented the rationale and thorough relationship on how the identified barriers could be eliminated by implementing the practices.

articleTitle: Application of Generative Artificial Intelligence to Assessment and Curriculum Design for Project-Based Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated generative AI learning literacy approach based on project-based learning to harness the transformative potential of generative AI in higher education. It provides a novel framework for integrating generative AI into project-based learning that aims to develop students' skills in three key aspects to grasp the application of generative AI as an effective problem-solving tool: (1) understanding algorithmic mechanisms, (2) identifying biases, and (3) using AI tools to solve problems. The process of integrating generative AI begins with assessing prior knowledge, introducing relevant problem-solving learning and AI tools, and designing course pathways and peer assessments through social media to cultivate students' problem-solving pathways. In addition, this paper recommends evaluating the effectiveness of AI-integrated courses through a comprehensive post-course survey of students and instructors.

articleTitle: Shining a Light on Collaboration: Enhancing Efficiency and Sustainability in Solar and Renewable Energy Supply Chains
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This research paper delves into the pivotal role of collaboration in enhancing efficiency and sustainability within solar and renewable energy supply chains. Employing a multi-method approach, the study investigates essential collaborative practices that drive operational efficiency, cost reduction, and sustainability improvements. It also examines the influential factors that either facilitate or hinder collaboration within these intricate supply chains. Notably, the paper underscores the significance of cross-sector collaborations, encompassing partnerships between industry, government, and academia, in attaining shared sustainability objectives. With the inclusion of real-world case studies and thorough analysis, the paper elucidates pathways toward more effective and sustainable renewable energy supply chains through the cultivation of dynamic collaboration.

articleTitle: Optimizing Atomic Layer Deposition Using a Hybrid of Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is a crucial technique in semiconductor miniaturization and high-precision applications. The quality of ALD processes directly affects the properties of the resulting thin films, leading to extensive evaluations for new ALD procedures. This study uses machine learning to quickly assess ALD process quality, with a focus on predicting the standard deviations of film thickness as an indicator of quality. Using a synthetic dataset simulating non-ideal ALD processes, we evaluated the performance of Random Forest Classifier (RFC), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN). We also introduced artificial neural network (ANN) and convolutional neural network (CNN) models for predicting standard deviations of film thickness from ALD trials. Our ANN and CNN models showed promising results, positioning them as reliable tools for predicting ALD process quality.

articleTitle: Bitcoin Mining Could Revolutionize Grid Computing and Unconventional Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Volunteer computing became popular during the late 1990s with software like SETI@home. In the early days of bitcoin mining, CPUs and GPUs were used similarly to volunteer computing: spare computing cycles are used to solve a problem (securing a blockchain in the case of cryptocurrency mining). Then came the specialized hardware of FPGAs and ASICs, and using CPUs and GPUs for bitcoin mining was not profitable anymore. We argue that bitcoin mining has revolutionized the development of specialized hardware and could continue doing so in the industry of unconventional computing. There is also a significant source of unused spare computing cycles in home computers and smartphones that could be used for grid computing purposes with the help of cryptocurrency mining. The notable result from our present analysis is the connection between cryptocurrency mining, grid/volunteer computing, and unconventional computing.

articleTitle: Mitigating Rate-Aware Jamming Attacks: A Deceptive Anti-Jamming Approach with Enhanced Utility
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Traditional anti-jamming strategies, such as frequency hopping and spread spectrum techniques, are insufficient in protecting the cognitive radio system from adaptive and intelligent jammers. To address this challenge, this article proposes a novel approach to anti-jamming based on deception techniques, which involves using a game-theoretic, pseudo-secondary user-based decoy to lure the jammer and deceive them into attacking a non-critical part of the network. In the proposed game-theoretic framework, the jammer's optimal strategy is to attack the decoy, while the network operator's optimal strategy is to protect the critical part of the network. By using a lure, the network operator can trick the jammer and achieve a Nash equilibrium where the jammer attacks the decoy, thereby protecting the communication system. Simulation results show that the proposed technique can improve the security of the communication system by increasing bandwidth efficiency, and decreasing the probability of a successful jamming attack.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Monitoring of Large-Scale 5G Technology Development
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Technology analysis and scouting is of great importance for appropriate management and development of innovation. It helps understand market trends and decide the direction of technology development for R&D planning purposes. This paper aims to track waves of innovations in the fifth generation (5G) technologies for mobile communication through patent analysis. It combines text mining techniques and regression analysis to reveal trends and hotspots of technology development. It also proposes a semi-supervised method to eliminate irrelevant documents from a large patent dataset. Results show a mapping of the 5G technological trends in 47 topics, which are identified by a topic model technique. The developed methodology can help firms identify important technological topics in 5G for making their R&D investment decisions. Firms can select appropriate technology strategies depending on the topic's emergence position in the topic strategy matrix.

articleTitle: Design of Hybrid Renewable Energy System for a Selected Location in Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The purpose of the current study is to constitute a structure for developing rural energy systems by evaluating the techno-economic viability of prospective hybrid energy systems (HES) for remote areas electrification like a hamlet in the district of Mastung, Pakistan. In Balochistan, the yearly direct mean radiation from the sun is between 7 to 7.5 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/day. However, it is closer to 4.5 to 5 kWh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/day in rest of Pakistan. The overall potential for wind energy in Pakistan is 346 GW. Initially, extensive resource evaluation has been done in the current study. To meet the peak-load requirement, system size optimization and techno-economic viability are then carried out by utilizing the HOMER Pro software. The electricity produced by wind and solar sources has been divided among the total load in the best possible way. The outcomes of the techno-economic analysis depict that HES is capable of producing more than 10 MW of power. With an annual AC main load of 12.8 GWh, the hybrid system generates 18.1 GWh of overall electricity. Wind turbines generate 1.3 GWh/yr with a proportion of 10.5%, whereas PV systems generate 9.8 GWh/yr with a fraction of 76.7%. The energy cost linked with commercial and residential sectors is taken into account depending on peak load demand patterns. A hybrid system costs ∃16.5 million and has an energy cost that is levelized at ∃0.0719 per kWh.

articleTitle: Methodology for Selection and Design of Sensor Systems for Mobile Service Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In the paper is described the selection of appropriate sensors and information systems for a Mobile Service Robot with collaborative functions requires a comprehensive methodology that takes into account the purpose of the robot, it's environment and the specific requirements of the applications to be used. This paper examines the role and features in the design of the Sensor Information System of this class of robots. The specifics of the sensor-information systems for the purposes of service robotics and the most commonly used sensors are discussed. A graphical representation of the algorithm for selecting suitable sensors for the purposes of the design task is presented. A variant of sensor classification for the needs of the developed algorithm is also included.

articleTitle: Unraveling the Complex Web of Energy Crises: Exploring Causes and Confronting Challenges in Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Pakistan, a nation nestled between South Asia and the Middle East, faces an enduring and formidable challenge: the energy crisis. The nation's rapid population growth, expanding economy, and increasing urbanization have placed immense pressure on its energy resources, leading to a persistent gap between demand and supply. As a consequence, the country grapples with frequent power outages, soaring energy costs, and hindered industrial growth, profoundly impacting its economic stability and the well-being of its citizens. This paper explores the in-depth current scenario of energy crises, causes, solutions, challenges and its impact on economy and society. This study also presents the existing initiatives and policy recommendations for sustainable energy management.

articleTitle: Real-Time 3D Multi-Person Pose Estimation Using an Omnidirectional Camera and mmWave Radars
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Learning-based monocular 3D human pose estimation holds significant potential for a variety of applications, including sports, automation, and entertainment; however, not always at a cost that allows it to be scaled. This paper proposes an affordable solution to learning-based monocular 3D pose estimation from 2D videos that can be utilised outdoors and indoors. We introduce a system that leverages an omnidirectional camera and mmWave radars to estimate the 3D pose of the people in the scene in real-time. The proposed algorithm shows good pose reconstruction accuracy with the average Euclidean distance between a ground truth body joint position and its 3D reconstruction ranging from 4.5cm to 19cm within 20 meters along both the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> axes of the camera.

articleTitle: Service Assurance in the Transport of Goods, to Encourage the Optimization of Processes Related to Transport Logistics and the Reduction of Waste
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: The transport of goods is one of the main economic activities today and an essential pillar of many other activities, with a well-defined growth trend and with increasingly demanding needs, namely in terms of quality of service, whether this is related to meeting deadlines or the conditions of carriage. This is particularly relevant when we talk about delicate, perishable goods of high commercial or even sentimental value. The paper proposes an architecture for carriers to provide a service with guaranteed transport conditions without major changes to the operating model and at a lower cost. Currently, this quality assurance is essentially based on validation, often empirical, of the state of the goods after delivery. It is not even possible to speak of confirmation upon delivery, as in reality, most operators avoid this confrontation. The existence of services with a guarantee of compliance with the agreed conditions for transport not only conveys the necessary confidence to the end customer, but can even promote other businesses, but above all promotes the accountability of all actors in the value chain, fostering process optimization and waste reduction. On the other hand, as this is a goods tracking solution, knowing the actual flow of goods helps identify opportunities for improvement. The architecture is based on IoT, cloud, and blockchain technologies.

articleTitle: Modified Fractional Edge Detection Masks Based on Compass Gradient for Retinopathy Screening
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Edge detection is pivotal in uncovering object boundaries and identifying discontinuities in digital images. This research paper proposes four novel edge detection techniques based on ABC-fractional integral using compass gradient masks, focusing on enhancing accuracy while maintaining reasonable computational effort. We thoroughly assess the results through visual evaluation by conducting extensive experiments on sample images from datasets such as BIPED, DRIVE, and HRF. Our findings demonstrate the superiority of the proposed methods over nine traditional and several recently introduced edge detection techniques. Moreover, we evaluate the performance of these algorithms using MSE, PSNR, SSIM, and EBIQA, demonstrating their promising potential for precise edge detection in Retinopathy images. Furthermore, concerning computational expenses, the fractional compass masks proposed in this study require nearly identical computational effort as the existing conventional masks.

articleTitle: Methodology for Designing a Collaborative Mobile Service Robot based on Criteria for Researching its Functional Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: In the article, based on the considered functional parameters of the robots, a Methodology for Designing a Manipulation System of a Service Robot for collaborative mobile services is proposed. The COVID-19 epidemic has shown that there are many sectors in the field of health care that can and should be robotized to ensure quality patient care and safe work for medical staff. The implementation of collaborative robots is a solution to this problem. The activities that robots can perform are diverse, and for each it is necessary to select a suitable collaborative service mobile robot that guarantees high reliability and safe operation. At the end of the article, a 3D model of a collaborative mobile robot designed to serve patients in children's clinics is).

articleTitle: Exploring Renewable Energy Resources Using GIS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Energy is the ability to perform work and is essential for all living processes. For its technological and cultural advancement, humanity has always relied on the usage of energy. In past few decades, the worldwide need for energy has risen, and most of the population around the globe depend heavily on non-renewable energy sources that includes oil, natural gas, and coal to generate energy. These non-renewable energy sources will soon run out and are environmentally destructive, which create the need for using alternative energy sources. The use of renewable energy resources has become the most significant way through which additional energy may be produced. The most important part of using renewable energy sources is to explore a number of good impacts like decreasing greenhouse gas emissions and reducing global warming. There are different renewable energy (RE) sources that are easily accessible like sun, wind, geothermal, tidal, biofuels etc. Faced with bleak predictions for energy supply and consumption, humanity is mobilizing massive efforts to acquire and grow renewable resources, as well as seek for cleaner, smarter, and more responsible energy generation, transmission, and distribution technologies. The geographic information system (GIS) is a computer application that helps in the understanding of topography and the making of best choices. GIS organizes geospatial information so that if anyone look at a map can quickly find the data they want for a specific purpose or task. GIS can help with RE integration in a variety of ways, including locating possible solar, biomass, and wind power plant sites, assessing RE potential at macro and micro scales using physical modelling, and studying the technical, economic, and social impacts of RE projects. GIS is transforming how we create and transmit energy, as well as how we view our planet's resources.

articleTitle: Automatic Calibration of the Driver's Gaze Area Based on a Semi-Supervised Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Driver's attention can be determined by monitoring the gaze area, which could be used to provide effective warnings. In practice, the height differences in drivers can affect the relative position between the camera and driver, which may increase the misrecognition of the gaze area.Aiming at resolving this problem, an automatic calibration method based on semi-supervised learning was proposed in the present study. To this end, the yaw and pitch of gaze were monitored based on the supervised learning model L2CS(L210ss cross-entropyloss softmax layer) network, and the line-of-sight reference frame was constructed by manual annotation. Then the highest density line-of-sight point area was calculated using the sliding window to complete the clustering. The performed analyses demonstrated that the performance index of gaze area monitoring significantly improves after calibration. It was found that the algorithm has promising non-perception and online repair characteristics,and the accuracy of gaze area classification is increased by 16% after using this calibration method.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable IDS Framework for Encrypted and Non-Encrypted Network Data in Supply Chains
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Supply Chains (SCs) constitute the bloodline for modern economic trade and manufacturing infrastructures. Their uninterrupted functionality remains of paramount importance. Consequently, substantial endeavors have been channeled into fortifying their security facets. This work presents an innovative solution to implement and integrate a well-established Intrusion Detection System (IDS) within the Supply Chain ecosystems. The proposed framework embodies an ingenuous way for merging an open-source and widely used network intrusion detection algorithm, Snort algorithm, with reconfigurable hardware technology, Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). The adoption of FPGAs confers notable advantages, as they enable the complete alleviation of high IDS workloads from Supply Chain servers. Moreover, the proposed framework possesses the ability to simultaneously check both non-encrypted and encrypted data traffic, thereby markedly amplifying the operational scope of the IDS. The final system performance evaluation shows that the proposed framework achieves network workload processing rate up to sixfold greater and energy consumption reduced by up to threefold when compared to the best optimized official software solution.

articleTitle: Hybrid Renewable Power Generation and Modeling (PV and Wind))
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Renewable energy sources (RES) are gaining significant traction in global electric power grids due to their potential for reducing carbon emissions and meeting increasing power demands. Hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbine (WT) storage systems have emerged as promising options for addressing these challenges. However, the occurrence of islanding situations, where renewable energy sources continue to supply power independently of the main grid, poses risks to utility workers' safety and system stability. To mitigate these concerns, this research presents a novel approach for enhancing islanding detection and power management in a hybrid PV-WT-battery system. The study proposes a modified maximum power point tracking algorithm incorporating a fractional order proportional integral (FOPI) controller to optimize power extraction from PV and wind systems under critical conditions. Additionally, an improved droop controller based on the maximum power of the PV system is introduced to ensure effective anti-islanding functionality and accurate power-sharing during islanded operation. The proposed control strategies are evaluated using Matlab R2021a software, demonstrating their efficacy in limiting DC link voltage and facilitating seamless mode transfer. Furthermore, the energy management system (EMS) is assessed in both grid-connected and islanded modes, validating the efficiency of the proposed droop control and EMS-based battery controller. Notably, the total harmonic distortion at the common coupling point is reduced to 1.98%, indicating improved power quality, while the hybrid system achieves an impressive overall efficiency of 97.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>.

articleTitle: Examining the Impact of Energy Management Systems on Energy Performance and Organizational Competitiveness: An Empirical Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: This study examines the impact of energy management systems (EnMS) on energy performance and organizational competitiveness. Manufacturing organizations were surveyed to collect data on EnMS implementation, energy consumption, and energy costs. The results of the study show that organizations with EnMS have lower energy consumption and costs than organizations without EnMS. The study also found that EnMS can improve organizational competitiveness by increasing productivity, reducing costs, and improving environmental performance. The findings of this study suggest that EnMS can be a valuable tool for organizations that are looking to improve their energy performance and competitiveness. The study also provides practical recommendations for organizations that are considering implementing an EnMS.

articleTitle: MIndex: an algorithm to predict the rebalancing of the ASX Index
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Forecasting stock additions and removals within the ASX 200 index holds significant implications for investors, enabling them to proactively adjust their portfolios and seize opportunities in response to market shifts. This preparedness also plays a crucial role in risk management by mitigating sudden fluctuations in portfolio value. Unfortunately, existing literature on index rebalancing is limited and not directly applicable to the ASX200. Until now, predictions for the ASX200 have relied solely on subjective methods. This paper introduces a novel algorithm called MIndex, designed specifically for forecasting ASX200 index changes, but extensible to other indices. MIndex leverages methodologies like ARIMA and incorporates AI techniques such as Prophet to provide a non-subjective approach to this forecasting process. It excels in accurately identifying stock additions and removals within the index. When compared to Macquarie's subjective predictions, MIndex outperforms in terms of F1-score and recall measures. This highlights MIndex's effectiveness in delivering actionable insights, strengthening strategic decision-making, and enhancing positioning within the dynamic landscape of index rebalancing.

articleTitle: How to Process, Model and Apply Heterogeneous Data Obtained from the IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Now, IoT systems generate massive amounts of data in diverse formats and shapes. Integrating information flows is essential for scientific, technical, and business practices. However, processing and using data in different formats and forms requires appropriate competencies, making it difficult to organize the entire process to achieve sustainable and reproducible results. Heterogeneity is one of the main characteristics of the data obtained from IoT systems, and this is the main reason for the problems arising in many cases of data analysis and application. This paper presents a systematized end-to-end methodology for processing, modelling and implementing heterogeneous data obtained from IoT devices. A general conceptual scheme of its development is offered. The theoretical-methodological framework is described and explained in detail as phases, grouped into four main stages. The pipelines are built by defining the stages, which show the necessary actions for each step. A systematized end-to-end methodology can be applied in different areas where IoT systems are used. The proposed end-to-end workflow is realized in the AWS cloud Serverless environment as a pipeline.

articleTitle: Invited Speakers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Engineering and Emerging Technologies (ICEET)
abstract: Thermal radiation represents a ubiquitous aspect of nature. Any object at finite temperatures emits thermal radiation due to thermally induced motion of particles and quasiparticles. The sun at 6000 K and the cold universe at 3 K, representing the most important renewable energy resource and the ultimate thermodynamic heat sink, are all accessible through thermal radiation. The ability to control thermal radiation therefore plays a fundamentally important role in energy applications. Nanophotonic structures, where at least one of the structural features are at a wavelength or sub-wavelength scale, can have thermal radiation properties that are drastically different from conventional thermal emitters, and offer exciting opportunities for energy applications. In this talk, I will discuss recent developments of nanophotonic control in thermal radiation, and highlight some exciting energy application opportunities, including radiative cooling and energy harvesting systems.
